title: Goal-side graph epoch advance for supersession
description:
Objective: give the goal aggregate a way to advance its graph epoch a SECOND time, so a superseded graph's successor can be recorded as the goal's active revision. Today the goal's epoch can only ever be 0 or 1.

Split from task-aedcd01ad91245d9a036d9dac3b76a22 by architect-8ee37119 on 2026-08-09. That task's own rail 2 required this split: the combined work needs 12+ distinct files against a 10-file hard cap, and the two halves share no file. This is the GOAL half (its DoD 1). The GRAPH REVISION half stays on task-aedcd01a and is being planned in parallel — the two touch disjoint directories, so they can run concurrently.

*** MEASURED ON DISK 2026-08-09 at HEAD 554d44c. Re-measure before planning; these claims are stale by default. ***

THE EPOCH AUTHORITY IS REAL AND LANDED — compose it, do not mint a second counter:
- `goal-contract.ts:130` — `readonly graphEpoch: number` on GoalState; `:155` on the GoalExecutionEnabled event.
- `goal-reducer.ts:94` — `goal.create` seeds `graphEpoch: 0` on DRAFT.
- `goal-reducer.ts:106-115` — `activate()` sets `graphEpoch: state.graphEpoch + 1`, rebinds `activeGraphRevisionRef`, moves DRAFT to EXECUTION_ENABLED, emits GoalExecutionEnabled carrying the epoch.
- `goal-reducer.ts:175` — `goal.reopen_as_revision` reseeds 0 on the new goal.
- `goal-validation.ts:228-238` — validates the epoch: safe integer, `>= 0`, DRAFT implies 0, COMPLETED implies `> 0`, active implies `> 0` with a valid `activeGraphRevisionRef`.

THE GAP, exactly one line wide: `goal-reducer.ts:40` admits `goal.activate_initial_graph` from `DRAFT` ONLY. No command advances the epoch from the live lifecycle, so a successor graph can never become the goal's active revision. `activate()` at :106 is very close to what is needed — the new handler differs mainly in its admitted lifecycle and in requiring a predecessor revision reference.

THE SIZING CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPES THIS TASK, measured with `grep -c ''`: `goal-reducer.ts` is 247 lines and `goal-validation.ts` is 245, both against a 250 target. There is NO room to add a handler or a predicate. This task therefore REQUIRES splitting a file before adding behavior. The obvious and precedented split: `goal-reducer.ts:48-85` holds seven inline result helpers (deepFreeze, rejected, unknownFailure, illegal, versionConflict, accepted, clonedState) that every other aggregate keeps in a separate module — see `packages/core/src/planning/planning-results.ts` and `graph-revision-results.ts`. Extracting them to a new `goal-results.ts` frees roughly 30 net lines and matches the established layout rather than inventing one.

BEWARE: `packages/core/src/goal/` is NOT swept by `planning-source-size.test.ts`, which covers `src/planning` only. A green core suite proves nothing about the per-file cap here, and two test files in this directory are ALREADY over 250 (`goal-reducer.test.ts` 300, `goal-invariants.test.ts` 281). Hand-measure every file you touch; do not take the suite's word for it.

DISAMBIGUATION, because the name collides: `goal-reducer.test.ts:53` defines an `ACTIVATION` const that is the goal's `InitialGraphActivationWitness` — a DIFFERENT type from the graph revision's activation witness that task-aedcd01a is changing. The two tasks do not share it.

Consumer, per the composition clause: task-aedcd01ad91245d9a036d9dac3b76a22 (Successor graph activation at predecessor epoch + 1) is the graph-revision half that binds to the epoch this command issues. Name it and record its id; a pure epoch advance with nothing binding it does not satisfy Clause 1.

NOT IN SCOPE: any change under packages/core/src/planning (that is task-aedcd01a), the graph revision activation witness, daemon persistence, scheduler wiring, UI.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test
definitionOfDone: A goal-side epoch advance exists: a new command kind admitted from the goal's live execution lifecycle increments `graphEpoch` by exactly 1 and rebinds `activeGraphRevisionRef` to the named successor revision, composing the landed counter pattern at goal-reducer.ts:110 rather than introducing a second epoch.

The command names the predecessor revision it replaces, and a command whose predecessor reference does not match the goal's current `activeGraphRevisionRef` refuses with an exact stable @moe/contracts code and the refusing layer, leaving state byte-identical.

A stale, equal, skipped or non-integer epoch cannot advance the goal; `goal.activate_initial_graph` remains admitted from DRAFT only and its behaviour is unchanged, proven by the pre-existing goal tests passing untouched.

Tests assert the exact reason code and refusing layer for every refusal path, a generated sweep asserts a non-zero case count, and a mutation drill proves each new guard is reddenable.

Do not add a second counter and do not move epoch authority out of the goal aggregate; the graph revision only ever persists a bound reference to the epoch it was activated at.

This task MUST split a file before it adds behavior. goal-reducer.ts is 247 lines and goal-validation.ts 245, both against a 250 target. Extract, then add — never grow either file past the cap and never take a green suite as evidence, because packages/core/src/goal/ is not swept by planning-source-size.test.ts.

Refusal tests assert the exact stable reason code AND which layer refused, never merely that the operation failed. @moe/contracts RuntimeError DROPS its validated `source`, so the layer must come from a production discriminant on the result — never from a test helper that reconstructs it. See graph-revision-results.ts for how the sibling aggregate solved this.
An epoch or predecessor reference that cannot be verified is UNKNOWN and refuses; it never defaults to 0, to 1, or to the current value.

Every pre-existing assertion in goal-reducer.test.ts and goal-invariants.test.ts must pass unchanged except those the new command genuinely invalidates. Both files are already over 250 lines; do not grow them further — put new coverage in a focused new test file.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED — create a NEW focused test file, packages/core/src/goal/goal-epoch-advance.test.ts. The rails forbid growing goal-reducer.test.ts (300 lines) or goal-invariants.test.ts (281); new coverage goes here.

Cases, each refusal pinning the EXACT stable @moe/contracts code AND the refusing layer read from the production result field, never reconstructed by a helper:
  - HAPPY PATH: from the live execution lifecycle, the new command increments graphEpoch by exactly 1 and rebinds activeGraphRevisionRef to the named successor. Assert the emitted event carries the new epoch, matching the :113 pattern.
  - PREDECESSOR MISMATCH (DoD 2): a command whose predecessor reference does not equal the goal's current activeGraphRevisionRef REFUSES, and state is BYTE-IDENTICAL afterwards. Assert the state object deep-equals the pre-command state — not merely that ok is false. A refusal that mutates is the defect worth catching.
  - STALE, EQUAL, SKIPPED and NON-INTEGER epochs each refuse (DoD 3). Assert each separately; collapsing them into one branch is how a skipped epoch later reads as merely stale.
  - UNKNOWN predecessor or epoch refuses and NEVER defaults to 0, to 1, or to the current value.
  - LIFECYCLE FENCE: the new command is NOT admitted from DRAFT, and goal.activate_initial_graph remains admitted from DRAFT ONLY with behaviour unchanged.

DoD 5: the generated sweep must assert a NON-ZERO case count — an emptied sweep must fail rather than pass silently.

Assert refusals by whole-object equality on { code, layer } so a swapped code or a missing layer fails.
